records.name: Laos in the House
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses storytelling and the arts to bring together Lao and Laotian Americans. It has run a summer camp for children that covers Lao music, dance, customs and cooking, keeps a volunteer sign-up form, and invites people to share their own stories.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer through the form on the site, send in a story through the submissions page, or come to an event the group announces. The group also sells merchandise and takes donations.

schedule.text: No regular weekly schedule is listed. The group announces events and its summer camp on the site as they are planned.

locations.label: Lao Buddhist Temple of North Philadelphia (site of the 2025 summer camp)

cost.text: Past summer camp prices were $75 for returning students and $125 for new students, and a place could be sponsored for $125. Donations and merchandise are also linked on the site.

first_step.how: Email info@laosinthehouse.com or fill in the volunteer sign-up form on the site. For the summer camp, watch the camp page and register there, since space is limited.
first_step.basis: The volunteer form and the camp registration are public and clear, but the site does not describe how to join its ongoing activities.
first_step.what_to_expect: The summer camp runs for one week, 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, with breakfast, lunch and snacks included. Campers are grouped by age and learn music, dance, customs, Lao phrases and cooking from teaching artists, then perform a recital at the end. Families can come on the first day.
first_visit_tips: The mailing address is c/o CultureTrust, so confirm the meeting place with the group before you visit
Register early, since the camp has limited space
Ask whether the next camp dates are set, because the site lists none yet

records.notes: Fetched 4 pages. The events page lists only 2023 events and the homepage shows no 2026 dates. The newest dated item is the summer camp, August 17 to 23, 2025, so last_sign_of_life is 2025-08 and status is probably_active. Tier 1 had no month for the camp; the camp page gives one. The 2025 camp was held at the Lao Buddhist Temple, recorded as a second location. Lao is not on the heritage list, so the community tag is asian_american. The volunteer form names skills (event coordination, outreach, translation) but shows no fields, time commitment or training. Language and access not stated on the pages read, so left out.

records.name: Neuroendocrine Tumor Support Group (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
records.summary: A monthly online group at Fox Chase Cancer Center for people with neuroendocrine tumors. Members learn coping skills and get support from others, which can help with loneliness and worry.
records.what_you_do: Join the online meeting on the third Wednesday, 4 to 5 pm, to talk with others and learn coping skills.

schedule.text: Third Wednesday of each month, 4 to 5 pm, online.

locations.label: Fox Chase Cancer Center (group meets online)

cost.text: Free. Fox Chase describes its support groups as a free service.

first_step.how: Call Fox Chase at 215-728-2668 (support group and social work questions) or the main line at 888-369-2427, and ask to join the neuroendocrine group. The group's page names two facilitators to contact.
first_step.basis: The page names facilitators to contact before you join, and it does not say who may join or what a session is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group meets online on the third Wednesday of each month from 4 to 5 pm, led by two licensed social workers. The page says sessions aim to reduce loneliness and anxiety, teach coping skills, and share practical information about treatment. Fox Chase's support pages say groups are for patients, their families and people in treatment elsewhere, but this page does not say who may join, so ask first.
first_visit_tips: Call the support line before the session to confirm how to join, since the page does not say
Ask for the printable schedule the group's page links to, to see the full year
Use a device with sound and a steady internet connection, since sessions are online

records.notes: The file id names the laryngectomy group, but the name, website and summary are the neuroendocrine group's, which is what was researched here. The tier 1 aka list shows 11 Fox Chase support groups merged under this one record; each has its own page on foxchase.org and the record should probably be split. Corrections: status changed from active to probably_active, and last_sign_of_life 2026-10 was removed because it came from the prostate group's page, a different group. The location label changed from the fireplace lounge to the campus address, since this group's page says it meets online. The index page says groups are for patients, families and people in treatment elsewhere; this page is silent, so open_to stays public with the caveat in what_to_expect. The Fox Chase events calendar showed no sessions (filter error). Checked for context only, not written as a record: the prostate group meets the second Thursday, 6:30 to 7:45 pm, in person with a Zoom option, and lists 2026 meetings.

records.name: LEGACY Youth Tennis & Education
records.summary: A tennis and education program based at the LEGACY Tennis Center on Ridge Avenue. It offers junior clinics, camps, private lessons, tournaments, and after-school programs at partner schools.
records.what_you_do: Kids join junior clinics, summer camps, and the after-school program. Adults can take clinics and lessons. Volunteers can coach in the after-school program, help at events, or join the summer program for a three-week term.

schedule.text: Junior clinics meet on the same day each week for a 13-week session. Summer camps run weekdays from 9 am to 3 pm for about 12 weeks.

cost.text: Prices are not listed on the pages read. Summer camps offer up to $25 a week off for early sign-up and 10 percent off each extra sibling, and need a 40 percent deposit to register. Financial aid is available for students whose families cannot cover fees.

first_step.how: Choose a junior clinic that fits your child's age on the junior clinics page, then register in the online Registration Portal. Adults can book private lessons on the lessons page.
first_step.basis: The Competitive Clinic accepts complete beginners, the Munchkin clinic is introductory, and registration is online. No trial class is offered, so it is not a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: Junior clinics meet on one set day each week for a 13-week session, grouped by age and level. Summer camps run weekdays from 9 am to 3 pm for about 12 weeks, and you can sign up week by week. The pages read do not list clinic prices, so check the portal or call before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Call 215.487.3477 to confirm the day and time for your child's clinic, since the junior clinics page does not list them
Ask whether a first clinic can be a trial, because the site does not say
If cost is a concern, the financial aid form is linked from the scholarships page

records.notes: Fetched 6 pages. Dropped the winter break camp: tier 1 used 2023 and 2024 pages, and the current camp page lists none. Dropped the contact name 'The Organization', a placeholder from the IRS file. Last sign of life is the June 19, 2026 Juneteenth celebration on the homepage. Financial aid for fall clinics session 2 is due October 16, 2026, and registration for session 2 opens October 26, 2026 (scholarships page). The after-school program runs at four Philadelphia public schools (McClure, Overbrook Educational Center, Wright and Pennell); the page gives no ages, days or cost, so no after-school schedule is written and the schools are not written as locations. All six junior clinics start 8/31/26, kept out of schedule text. Summer camp dates on the page carry no year, so none is written. Volunteer questions go through the contact form on the volunteer page.

records.name: Leveling the Playing Field (Philadelphia)
records.summary: A youth sports charity that collects donated sports gear and gives it free to schools and programs that serve kids in under-resourced communities. Volunteers sort and check gear at its Philadelphia warehouse in Sharon Hill.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers book a shift of about two hours, by appointment, to sort and inventory donated gear, check that it is in good shape, and keep the warehouse in order. Individuals and groups may sign up. Volunteers must be at least 10, and an adult must come with anyone under 15.

schedule.text: The drop-off bin outside the warehouse is open 24 hours a day. Volunteer shifts are booked by appointment, and pick-ups need prior approval. Days and months of operation are not stated.

cost.text: Donated gear is free to approved programs. The grant gives access to donated gear only, not money. The pages read do not state a cost to volunteer.

first_step.how: To volunteer, book a shift through the VolunteerHub link on the volunteer page, or email info@levelingtheplayingfield.org. To get gear, a school or sports program submits the online grant application, which is reviewed before a site call or visit.
first_step.basis: Volunteer shifts are booked online through a clear route. No training is required, though basic knowledge of sports gear is preferred. The gear grant is for programs, not individual families.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shift lasts about two hours at the Sharon Hill warehouse. You sort donated gear, check that it is in usable shape, and help keep the shelves in order. No training is required, and individuals and groups both come.
first_visit_tips: The warehouse is in Sharon Hill, outside the city, so plan travel time
Anyone under 15 must come with an adult, and volunteers must be at least 10
Book your shift in advance, since volunteering is by appointment only

records.notes: Corrected tier 1: gear goes to programs (schools, recreation centers, after-school programs and nonprofits serving children in under-resourced communities), and the apply page does not name individual families as eligible. Pick-up is in person only, with 24 hours notice. The warehouse is in Sharon Hill, Delaware County, outside city limits. Kept as publish because the group calls it its Philadelphia warehouse and the Philadelphia volunteer center page is the source. FAQ: volunteer time at warehouses can count toward service-learning hours and the group is approved to sign for them; service_hours_letter is left unknown because the pages do not say it issues a letter. The general info address is info@levelingtheplayingfield.org (FAQ). The volunteer page notes that its email link points to a Washington address, so the Philadelphia address is the one recorded.

records.name: Leverington Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on Ridge Avenue with Sunday worship also streamed on YouTube and small programs, including a lunch series, a games and dinner night, and a men's coat drive.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the Lunch Bunch lunch series, the Games, Gab and Grub night, a small group, or a women's retreat. Use the Connect With Us form to get started.

schedule.text: Sunday worship, also streamed on YouTube. Service times are not stated on the pages read, so confirm them with the office. Lunch Bunch and Games, Gab and Grub run as short series with set dates on their registration pages.

locations.label: Majer Home, Plymouth Meeting (2026 Games, Gab and Grub host site)

cost.text: Costs are not listed for Lunch Bunch or Games, Gab and Grub. Call the office to ask before you register.

first_step.how: Register for Lunch Bunch or Games, Gab and Grub on the church's sign-up pages, or use the Connect With Us form to ask about a group. You can also call the office at 215-482-0293.
first_step.basis: The planning page says there is no dress code and that the service guides visitors through each step, and the Connect With Us form is the way in for groups.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is also streamed on YouTube, so you can watch first from home. The planning page says there is no dress code and that the service guides visitors through each step. Service times are not stated on the pages read, so call the office to confirm before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at 215-482-0293 to confirm the Sunday service time
Ask the office about parking and accessibility, since the site does not say
Watch a service on YouTube first if you want to see the format before visiting

records.notes: Service time not confirmed: no page read states it. A search snippet from the church's site gave conflicting times (9:30 and 10:30 am across entries), and the home church page linked from search returned a 404, so no time is written. The office should confirm. The ministries page lists only community organizations, children's ministries and international missions, so the lunch series and games night come from Church Center registration pages. Status moved to active because Lunch Bunch (October 28 to December 16, 2026) and Games, Gab and Grub (November 1 and December 6, 2026) are listed with 2026 dates. Games, Gab and Grub's 2026 dates are hosted at a home in Plymouth Meeting, outside the city, recorded as a second location. The men's coat drive and women's retreat have no dates, cost or location on the pages read. The Sunday schedule page linked from the planning page was not opened.

records.name: Lighthouse 1893
records.summary: A Fairhill community organization founded in 1893 as a preschool and afterschool program. It runs youth sports leagues, a STEM program for kids 8 to 13, and Recreation Over Violence, an affordable sports program for children and families. Its Lions Elite teams play at several age levels.
records.what_you_do: Kids can join sports leagues, the STEM program or the summer camp. Families can take part in Recreation Over Violence. Adults can volunteer through an online form, and membership is a monthly donation that funds the programs.

schedule.text: Sports leagues and programs run year-round, according to the site. Days, times and seasons are not stated on the pages read.

cost.text: Program fees are not stated. Membership is a monthly donation, from $10 a month (SPARK) to $100 a month (LIGHTKEEPER), with higher tiers above that. The page does not say whether a child needs a membership to play.

first_step.how: Call 215-425-7800, the number the site lists for getting started, and ask about the league, the STEM program or Recreation Over Violence. For the 2026 STEM program, use the enrollment button on its page.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone number and a membership page, but does not say how children sign up, when programs start, or whether there is a tryout, so the way in takes an extra step.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical practice, class or session length. The 2026 STEM program for kids aged 8 to 13 covers six weekly topics, including body systems, brain science and movement. Ask the phone line about start dates, cost and whether a child needs a membership to play.
first_visit_tips: Call before you visit, since the site does not list program times
Ask whether a membership is needed before a child can play
Check which building your program uses: the Somerset Building or the Lighthouse Sports Complex

records.notes: Fetched 6 pages. Kind changed from club to nonprofit, since it is a donation-funded community organization. Tier 1 said mentoring is delivered through Recreation Over Violence, but that page describes affordable sports and family anti-violence resources and no mentorship, so the mentoring tag was removed and the STEM tag added from the STEM page. The STEM page says the preschool has closed while the afterschool activities continue, which supports the summary. Membership tiers are donations per the Champions page. Ages, days and times are stated only for the STEM program (8 to 13). Last sign of life 2026-06 comes from post dates in the URL paths of the homepage (2026/05/19 and 2026/06/01), not from text on the page. The volunteer form is a Google form linked from the volunteer page and was not opened.

records.name: Limitless Ladies Ministries
records.summary: A Christ-centered nonprofit ministry for women. It runs Love Bags, care packages of everyday supplies and encouraging notes for people in need, plus teen workshops and life coaching.
records.what_you_do: Ask about a teen workshop by phone or email, or ask how to help with Love Bags. The events page lists past workshops, and the site's Schedule a Workshop button has no working link.

schedule.text: Workshops and events are announced on the events page when they are planned. None were listed for 2026 when the page was read.

cost.text: The pages read do not say whether workshops cost money. The online store sells items that help fund the Love Bags and workshops, and donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Call 302-468-7234 or email slfowlkes@limitlessladiesforever.org to ask about the next teen workshop or about helping with Love Bags.
first_step.basis: The events page shows no current workshops, the booking button has no link, and the way in is a phone call or email, so the first step is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a workshop runs or what it costs. Past teen workshops in 2025 were held on Saturdays and covered topics such as mental health and a friendship bracelet craft.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you come, since the site does not show upcoming workshops
Ask whether a workshop is for teens or adults, and whether a parent should come
Ask for the location, since the site gives only a PO box address

records.notes: Fetched 4 pages. The homepage lists the email and phone above, but the contact page lists neither and shows only a form, and the email domain (limitlessladiesforever.org) differs from the website domain. Verify before publishing. The events page lists only 2025 events (April 12, April 26, May 31 and August 30, 2025); the August 30 entry has no venue or details, so last_sign_of_life is 2025-08 and status stays probably_active. The 2025 workshops were held at the PO box address and at a partner site in 19142 named on the events page, so the group has no meeting place of its own. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because no current workshops are listed and the booking button has no link. The faith tradition is not stated beyond Christian, so faith is left out. Fathership Foundation is named as the host of the April 26, 2025 workshop and is listed in leads_only.
